activity.notes: Contemporary Shang oracle-bone evidence records Fu Hao in military activity, while her intact Yinxu tomb contained weapons and insignia associated with command. ATLAS records a broad approximate c.1250-c.1200 BCE military-activity interval because individual campaign dates are not securely reducible to one exact modern year range.

sources.title: Hello, Yinxu⑥丨Tomb of China's First Female General, Fu Hao.
sources.citation_text: The People's Government of Henan Province, 'Hello, Yinxu⑥丨Tomb of China's First Female General, Fu Hao.', 2023. The article identifies Fu Hao as a consort of Shang king Wu Ding and a female military leader, and describes her intact Yinxu tomb and its agreement with oracle-bone records.
sources.locator: Fu Hao described as China's first known female general overseeing external military affairs

sources.title: War and Sacrifice: The Tomb of Fu Hao
sources.citation_text: Cortney E. Chaffin, Smarthistory, 'War and Sacrifice: The Tomb of Fu Hao.' The study synthesizes oracle-bone inscriptions and archaeological evidence for Fu Hao as a royal consort, military commander, ritual practitioner, and administrator in the thirteenth century BCE.
sources.locator: Who was Fu Hao?; discussion of oracle-bone military command and weapons from Tomb 5
